Multiply the equation by $1001 = 7\cdot 11\cdot 13$, the LCM of $77, 91, 143$:

$$13a + 11b + 7c = 1001.$$

Adding $13b + 13c$ to both sides and rearranging gives

$$13(a+b+c) = 1001 + 2b + 6c,$$

so $S = a+b+c = \dfrac{1001 + 2(b+3c)}{13}$. Minimizing $S$ means minimizing $T = 2(b+3c)$.

Since $1001 + T$ must be divisible by 13, $T$ must be a multiple of 13. Since $T$ is even, $T$ must be a multiple of 26. With $b, c \ge 1$, the smallest possible value is $T = 26$, which requires $b + 3c = 13$.

The options are $(b,c) = (10,1), (7,2), (4,3), (1,4)$. Each gives a positive integer $a$:
- $(b,c)=(10,1)$: $13a = 1001 - 110 - 7 = 884$, so $a = 68$.
- $(b,c)=(7,2)$: $13a = 1001 - 77 - 14 = 910$, so $a = 70$.
- $(b,c)=(4,3)$: $13a = 1001 - 44 - 21 = 936$, so $a = 72$.
- $(b,c)=(1,4)$: $13a = 1001 - 11 - 28 = 962$, so $a = 74$.

Each gives $S = (1001+26)/13 = 79$. For example, $(a,b,c) = (68,10,1)$ checks out: $13\cdot 68 + 11\cdot 10 + 7\cdot 1 = 884 + 110 + 7 = 1001$.

So the minimum is $a+b+c = 79$.

ANSWER: 79
